title: Compatible discrete Maxwell constraints and finite algorithms

items.title: Finite cochain Maxwell phase space
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix nonnegative integers $n_0,n_1,n_2,n_3$ and ordered coordinate bases, and put $C^k:=\mathbb R^{n_k}$ for $k=0,1,2,3$. The dual space $(C^k)^*$ is the vector space of linear functionals $C^k\to\mathbb R$, with the dual basis to the chosen coordinate basis. Let $D_0\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times n_0}$, $D_1\in\mathbb R^{n_2\times n_1}$, and $D_2\in\mathbb R^{n_3\times n_2}$ be linear maps satisfying $D_1D_0=0$ and $D_2D_1=0$. This data is a finite cochain complex. The transpose $D_k^{\mathsf T}$ denotes the representing matrix of the dual linear map in the dual bases. Let $M_1\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times n_1}$ and $M_2\in\mathbb R^{n_2\times n_2}$ be symmetric positive-definite matrices: $v^{\mathsf T}M_kv>0$ for each nonzero $v\in C^k$. They represent linear maps $M_1:C^1\to(C^1)^*$ and $M_2:C^2\to(C^2)^*$ in the chosen bases; in positive dimensions their inverses exist by the finite-dimensional positive-matrix result cited below, and the unique map on a zero-dimensional space is its own inverse.

The finite state space is $\mathcal X:=C^2\oplus(C^1)^*$, with state $(b,d)$, where $b$ is a column of $C^2$ coordinates and $d$ is a column in the dual basis of $(C^1)^*$. In this item, “phase space” means this finite-dimensional state space only; no symplectic form is asserted. On an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, a semidiscrete trajectory is a continuously differentiable map $t\mapsto(b(t),d(t))\in\mathcal X$ satisfying

$$\dot b(t)=-D_1M_1^{-1}d(t),\qquad \dot d(t)=D_1^{\mathsf T}M_2b(t).$$

Its two discrete constraints are $D_2b(t)=0$ in $C^3$ and $D_0^{\mathsf T}d(t)=0$ in $(C^0)^*$. The associated quadratic energy is

$$\mathcal E(b,d):=\tfrac12\left(b^{\mathsf T}M_2b+d^{\mathsf T}M_1^{-1}d\right).$$

All objects here are finite-dimensional real linear-algebra data. The term “Maxwell” names this algebraic model and does not identify it with a continuum Maxwell or Einstein–Maxwell solution.

items.title: Finite compatible leapfrog evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the finite cochain data fixed by the preceding definition item, namely finite real coordinate spaces $C^0,C^1,C^2,C^3$, maps $D_0,D_1,D_2$ with $D_1D_0=D_2D_1=0$, and symmetric positive-definite mass maps $M_1,M_2$. Inputs are rational matrices $D_0,D_1,D_2,M_1,M_2$, rational initial coordinates $b_0\in C^2$ and $d_{1/2}\in(C^1)^*$, a positive rational step size $\tau$, and an integer $N\geq0$. The matrices and states use the fixed ordered bases and dual bases from that definition. All arithmetic is exact over $\mathbb Q$; floating-point arithmetic is not part of this algorithm.

First compute $R=M_1^{-1}$ once by fixed-order, no-row-swap Gauss–Jordan elimination of the augmented matrix $[M_1\mid I_{n_1}]$. For each pivot column $j=1,\ldots,n_1$, let $p$ be the current entry in position $(j,j)$. If $p=0$, return an inconsistency error. Otherwise divide row $j$ by $p$ and, for every $k\neq j$, replace row $k$ by row $k$ minus its current column-$j$ entry times row $j$. After all columns are processed, let $R$ be the right block. For $n_1=0$, take the unique empty matrix for $R$ and perform no elimination.

Set $(b,d):=(b_0,d_{1/2})$ and record this initial state. For each $n=0,\ldots,N-1$, in the stated order compute

$$b_{\mathrm{new}}:=b-\tau D_1Rd,\qquad d_{\mathrm{new}}:=d+\tau D_1^{\mathsf T}M_2b_{\mathrm{new}}.$$

Append $(b_{\mathrm{new}},d_{\mathrm{new}})$ to the output list and then set $(b,d):=(b_{\mathrm{new}},d_{\mathrm{new}})$. After the loop, return $R$ together with the list of the $N+1$ states $(b_n,d_{n+1/2})$ for $0\leq n\leq N$. The error branch is unreachable on admissible inputs; the separate finite-step termination lemma proves this and the exact inverse output.

items.title: Exact discrete constraints and semidiscrete and staggered energy
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use finite-dimensional real cochain data as in the definition item and fix $\tau>0$. For a state $(b,d)\in\mathcal X$, define the real one-step map $T_\tau:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ by

$$b^+:=b-\tau D_1M_1^{-1}d,\qquad d^+:=d+\tau D_1^{\mathsf T}M_2b^+,\qquad T_\tau(b,d):=(b^+,d^+).$$

On rational admissible matrices, rational initial coordinates, and rational $\tau>0$, this is the one-step update used by the exact rational algorithm; the algorithm's input domain is the rational one stated in its Definition. For every real input state, $D_2b^+=D_2b$ and $D_0^{\mathsf T}d^+=D_0^{\mathsf T}d$, so an input satisfying both zero constraints maps to a state satisfying both. Every continuously differentiable semidiscrete solution conserves $\mathcal E(b,d)$. For any sequence $(b_n,d_{n+1/2})_{n\geq0}$ with $(b_{n+1},d_{n+3/2})=T_\tau(b_n,d_{n+1/2})$, define

$$Q_\tau(b,d):=b^{\mathsf T}M_2b+d^{\mathsf T}M_1^{-1}d-\tau b^{\mathsf T}M_2D_1M_1^{-1}d,\qquad Q_n:=Q_\tau(b_n,d_{n+1/2}).$$

Then $Q_n$ is exactly invariant under $T_\tau$. Equip coordinate and dual-coordinate columns with their standard Euclidean inner products, so $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}y$ and $\lVert x\rVert_2=(x^{\mathsf T}x)^{1/2}$. Regard $S:=M_2^{1/2}D_1M_1^{-1/2}$ as a real linear map from the dual-coordinate columns of $(C^1)^*$ to the coordinate columns of $C^2$. Set $\sigma:=0$ when its domain $(C^1)^*$ is zero; otherwise set $\sigma:=\max_{\lVert y\rVert_2=1}\lVert Sy\rVert_2$. For a nonzero domain this is the largest singular value of $S$. The quadratic form $Q_\tau$ is positive definite on $\mathcal X$ whenever $\tau\sigma<2$.

items.title: Finite arithmetic termination and cost
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For rational admissible input matrices and initial state, positive rational step size $\tau$, and finite $N\geq0$, the specified finite leapfrog algorithm returns after finitely many exact rational arithmetic operations, with the stated $N+1$ states and the exact rational inverse $M_1^{-1}$. A dense implementation uses $O(n_1^3)$ rational arithmetic operations for the one-time elimination and $O(n_1^2+n_1n_2+n_2^2)$ per update. Retaining all input matrices $D_0,D_1,D_2,M_1,M_2$, the computed inverse, and all $N+1$ states uses $O(n_1n_0+n_1^2+n_1n_2+n_2^2+n_2n_3+(N+1)(n_1+n_2))$ rational entries. These are arithmetic-operation and storage counts only; they give no bound on rational bit growth, floating-point roundoff, linear-solve residuals, or continuum accuracy.

items.title: Constraint preservation does not imply bounded leapfrog evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: The statement refuted is: for every finite cochain datum of the type defined in the item named “Finite cochain Maxwell phase space,” every positive rational step size in the item named “Finite compatible leapfrog evolution,” and every initial state satisfying $D_2b_0=0$ and $D_0^{\mathsf T}d_{1/2}=0$, repeated application of its one-step map has a bounded orbit. Here “bounded orbit” means that the Euclidean norm of the coordinate vector $(b_n,d_{n+1/2})$ has finite supremum over all integers $n\geq0$.
